about.title: Martinez Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Martinez sees its share of collisions along Alhambra Avenue, SR-4, and I-680, with Contra Costa County records showing 116 injury collisions and 141 injured people in the most recent reported year. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to bring more reported crashes, likely tied to commuters heading home or to the Amtrak station and downtown. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the period right after matters — insurers move fast, and what you say to them can shape your claim before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive isn't a law firm; we're a free service that connects injured people in Martinez with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the facts, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid common missteps with insurance adjusters. There's no cost to get connected, and no pressure to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Statute of Limitations Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a claim, but if a government entity or roadway defect is involved — say, near an SR-4 interchange — that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce What You Recover
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your compensation gets reduced by your share of blame. An early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to inflate your percentage of fault, so it helps to have guidance before you speak with them.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering, No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and attorneys in our network work on contingency — meaning there's no fee unless you recover money. That structure lets you pursue a claim without adding financial risk while you're already dealing with medical bills.

items.question: I was in a crash near the SR-4/I-680 interchange in Martinez. Does it matter who owns the road?
items.answer: It can. If a design or maintenance issue involving Caltrans or a local agency contributed to the crash, you may be dealing with a government claim, which typically carries a much shorter filing deadline — sometimes just six months. An attorney can help identify whether that applies to your situation and act quickly if so.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You're generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it's often better not to until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to shift fault onto you, which matters under California's comparative fault rules. A quick conversation with an attorney first can help protect your claim.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and we don't charge you to connect with an independent attorney. If you move forward and the attorney takes your case, they typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
